basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es, et cur concidit facies tua? Nonne si bene'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es, et cur concidit facies tua? Nonne si bene egeris, recipies; sin autem male, statim in foribus peccatum tuum aderit? Quare, inquit, irasceris, et invidiae in fratrem livore cruciaris, vultum dimittis in terram? Nonne si bene egeris, si pura mente sacrificium obtuleris, recipies, respiciente Domino ad te et ad sacrificium tuum: sin autem male egeris, statim in foribus peccatum tuum aderit, et tali janitore intrans semper exiensque comitaberis, pro eo ut Dominus custodiret introitum tuum et exitum tuum, et sicut de sapientia dicitur: Qui de luce vigilaverit ad illam non laborabit. Assidentem enim illam in foribus suis inveniet (Sap. VI, 15). Et iterum: Quoniam dignos se ipsa circuit quaerens, et in viis ostendit se illis habitator, et in omni providentia occurrit illis (Ibid., 17).
